newsitem.title: POLAND: Three Polish insurers sign cooperation agreement.
newsitem.headline: Three Polish insurers sign cooperation agreement.

text.p: Three Polish insurers, state-owned Powszechny Zaklad Ubezpieczen SA (PZU), TUiR Warta and TUR Polisa, have signed a cooperation agreement on insuring large risks, Polisa's deputy president said on Tuesday.
Zygfryd Kielarski told Reuters the deal provided for insuring risks of more than $100 million jointly.
"Under the agreement, we will offer our clients insurance deals together in cases when none of us could do it on its own," he said.
He added that under the agreement PZU would take 60 percent of the risk involved, Warta 30 percent and Polisa 10 percent.
The accord is specifically designed to enable the three companies to insure projects under Poland's $8 billion scheme to build 2,500 km of motorways over the next 15 years.
He added PZU, Warta and Polisa also planned cooperation in other areas but refused to give details.
